jobs.title: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor of Communication (Review begins: 10/15/26)
statuses: Job description: The Department of Communication at Rollins College invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Communication beginning August 2027. We seek a scholar-teacher who uses high-impact educational practices to prepare students for responsible leadership and global citizenship, including service learning, community engagement, interdisciplinary collaboration, and student-faculty research. The successful candidate will teach foundational courses in the Communication major, including COM 100: Introduction to Communication, COM 285: Research Methods, and/or COM 480: Senior Seminar (capstone course), and will have the opportunity to develop electives in their area of expertise. Areas of interest may include persuasion, communication theory, civic engagement, crisis communication, digital media, artificial intelligence and emerging communication technologies, or other areas where communication intersects with global challenges. The successful candidate will also contribute to the College’s general education program.

jobs.snippet: Professor of Practice, Operations, Technology, and Information Management Cornell SC Johnson College of Business Cornell University The Cornell SC Johnson College of Business invites applicants for a Professor of Practice position with 50 – 100% appointment in our Operations, Technology, and Information Management (OTIM) area, with a school affiliation in the Johnson Graduate School of Management.
jobs.detailText: Professor of Practice, Operations, Technology, and Information Management Cornell SC Johnson College of Business Cornell University The Cornell SC Johnson College of Business invites applicants for a Professor of Practice position with 50 – 100% appointment in our Operations, Technology, and Information Management (OTIM) area, with a school affiliation in the Johnson Graduate School of Management. The intended start date of this position is July 1, 2027. The position will be based in Ithaca, NY. Responsibilities of the position include teaching MBA courses in Operations Strategy, Experience in Strategic Operations, and other related graduate courses in the college. The ideal candidate will possess a PhD in business or a related field and have relevant prior work experience in a senior leadership role in industry. Candidates holding a master's degree in business or a closely related field, along with relevant teaching experience, will also be considered. It is expected that our faculty teach across multiple schools within the College of Business. The Cornell SC Johnson College of Business (established on July 1, 2016) combines three Schools: the Samuel Curtis Johnson Graduate School of Management (Johnson), the Charles H. Dyson School of Applied Economics and Management (Dyson), and the Nolan School of Hotel Administration (Nolan). The Samuel Curtis Johnson Graduate School of Management offers MBA, Accelerated MBA, Executive MBA, and Ph.D. programs. Courses and programs are taught at Cornell's main Ithaca campus, the Cornell Tech campus in New York City, and other locations across the globe. To be considered for this position, apply at https://academicjobsonline.org/ajo/jobs/33006 . For full consideration please ensure that your application is complete by October 31, 2026. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position has been filled. Applications received after October 31, 2026 will be reviewed if the position has not been filled. The following materials are required: 1. Letter of interest, with clear indication of position being applied for; 2. Curriculum vitae; 3. Up to three research papers; 4. Three recommendation letters; 5. Report of courses taught and evidence of teaching effectiveness; and 6. Any other supporting documents, such as curriculum development materials Consistent with Cornell's practice, appointment to academic positions requires candidates to disclose relevant information about their prior employment including whether they have been found to have violated institutional or employer policies related to or governing unlawful discrimination and harassment, academic and research misconduct, or financial misconduct. In compliance with New York's Pay Transparency Act, the minimum annual base salary range for this position is $120,000 - $280,000. This pay range represents base pay only (for 9 months, paid over 12 months) and excludes any additional items such as incentives, bonuses, or other items. Cornell University considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate's work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, as well as market and organizational considerations when extending an offer. Send job Job Details Company Job Details Job Description Virginia Tech’s Department of English invites applications for a
full-time, tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant
or Associate Professor in Technical and Scientific Communication.
This position reflects Virginia Tech's strategic commitment to
understanding not only how technologies are developed, but how they
are implemented, communicated, trusted, and integrated into
organizations and communities, with a particular focus on
healthcare. We seek an innovative scholar whose work advances the
future of technical and scientific communication in an era
increasingly defined by artificial intelligence, automation,
immersive technologies, and complex sociotechnical systems. We seek
a scholar whose research and teaching examine how communication
shapes the design, implementation, and use of emerging technologies
in professional, organizational, scientific, technical, or
healthcare environments. This position is associated with Virginia Tech’s Smart Healthcare
Hub initiative (smarthealthcare.icat.vt.edu) and will contribute to
the growth of interdisciplinary research, innovation, and teaching
at the intersection of emerging technologies, healthcare-related
simulations, digital and/or medical humanities, experience design,
operations, and human-centered systems. The successful candidate
will join a highly multidisciplinary and collaborative environment
that values innovation, experiential learning, translational
research, and community engagement. The successful candidate will
contribute to Virginia Tech's internationally recognized Technical
and Scientific Communication program as a member of the Department
of English while engaging in interdisciplinary research
collaborations across the university. Given the expectation that the position will involve high research
productivity and pursuit of research funding as part of the Smart
Healthcare Hub initiative, the position will begin with a teaching
assignment of two courses per academic year (one in fall and one in
spring) that includes teaching in the Department of English’s
undergraduate Technical and Scientific Communication and the
doctoral Rhetoric and Writing programs. After three years, the
teaching assignment is expected to increase to the department’s
typical teaching assignment for tenure-track and tenured faculty of
four courses each academic year (two in fall and two in
spring). Position Overview The ideal candidate for this position will help define the future
of the discipline by advancing research that improves communication
across complex technical, scientific, healthcare, governmental, or
industrial contexts. We welcome applicants whose scholarship addresses one or more areas
including, but not limited to: Ethics of emerging technologies Rhetoric of science, technology, and medicine Digital and/or medical humanities Human-centered design Technical communication and artificial intelligence Accessibility and inclusive design Science writing The department particularly values scholars whose work bridges
traditional disciplinary boundaries and who are skilled at
collaborating with researchers across engineering, computer
science, health sciences, business, public policy, and the
humanities. We seek an individual that has expertise in applying
their work within the healthcare sector. Responsibilities The successful candidate will maintain an active, externally
visible research program, including work associated with the Smart
Healthcare Hub’s focus; contribute to undergraduate and graduate
education; mentor students; and participate in departmental,
college, and university service. Primary responsibilities include: Research Develop and sustain a nationally recognized program of
scholarship in technical and scientific communication. Publish in leading journals and present research at national
and international conferences. Pursue externally funded research opportunities and contribute
to collaborative external funding proposals. Build interdisciplinary collaborations across Virginia Tech and
with external partners. Mentor graduate and undergraduate student researchers. Teaching Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in technical and
scientific communication and rhetoric, including foundational and
advanced courses that may include grant writing; medical and
science writing; the rhetoric of science, technology, and medicine;
document design; visual rhetoric; and/or digital rhetoric. Faculty
are encouraged to develop new courses aligned with their expertise
and emerging areas of the discipline. Service The successful candidate will contribute to the continued growth of
Virginia Tech's nationally recognized Technical and Scientific
Communication program through curriculum development, student
mentoring, program leadership, and university service while
participating in national professional organizations. Collaborative Opportunities Virginia Tech offers exceptional opportunities for
interdisciplinary collaboration. The successful candidate will have
opportunities to engage with faculty across the College of Liberal
Arts and Human Sciences, College of Engineering, College of
Science, Virginia Tech Carilion School of Medicine, Pamplin College
of Business, and numerous university-wide research institutes and
centers such as the Institute for Society, Culture, and
Environment, Institute for Creativity, Arts, and Technology, the
Fralin Biomedical Research Institute, and the Whole Health
Consortium. How to Apply Screening of applications will begin November 15, 2026. For full
consideration, all materials must be submitted prior to this date.
Please submit: A CV A Cover Letter A detailed statement detailing teaching/mentoring
philosophy A detailed statement of research accomplishments and plans Names and contact information for 3 professional references;

pedagogies, and the integration of emerging disciplinary and

vitality, and sharing professional expertise within and beyond the

certificate in science writing and design, and a large general
education writing program, serving nearly 4,000 students per

emphases on technical, digital, visual, medical/health, social
justice, and community-based rhetoric and professional writing.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Sports Media and Communication (Deadline: 11/09/2026).
statuses: Job description: The Drake School of Journalism and Mass Communication invites applications for a nine-month, consecutive term appointment of an assistant professor of sports media and communication, beginning in fall semester 2027. Professional experience working in sports media is required. Ideally the candidate will have experience in sports production and live broadcasts. Candidates may also bring front-of-camera experience to the role. A portfolio of work is expected. Evidence of teaching effectiveness is preferred. Master's degree is preferred, but we are open to hiring an experienced professional with a bachelor's degree for this consecutive-term appointment. Qualified candidates will have a demonstrated ability to train and mentor students and a history of early adoption of new technologies. The qualified candidate may also teach online graduate classes in Digital Media Strategies, Emerging Media, and Multimedia Storytelling. Course load is seven courses (4/3) over the academic year. Duties also include academic and career mentoring for students, advising a student media organization or student sports production, and service to the University and community.

Send job Job Details About Wenzhou-Kean University Wenzhou-Kean University (WKU), located in Wenzhou, China, one of three Sino-American universities along with NYU Shanghai and Duke Kunshan University, is approved by the Ministry of Education of China. Launched in 2012, WKU offers a unique model of higher education in partnership with Kean University, a comprehensive, public university in the state of New Jersey that is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education. WKU sits on approximately 500 beautiful acres and currently enrolls about 5,500 undergraduate and graduate students, and it is now in the midst of a rapid growth that will bring enrollment to 7,000 students within the next three years. All instruction is in English, and all curriculum is provided by Kean University. In addition to its current 18 undergraduate programs, WKU has been approved by the Ministry of Education for offering 14 Master s and 3 doctorate programs including the M.A. in Communication. WKU highly values research-powered teaching and learning, and the average number of faculty publications and the Field-weighted Citation Impact are among the best of leading Chinese academic institutions. Wenzhou is one of the most vibrant and economically advanced developed cities on China s East Coast, located one hour by plane and three hours by high-speed train from Shanghai Position: The College of Liberal Arts is seeking highly motivated individuals to join the Communication department at WKU. All faculty positions are full-time assignments, effective for the year of 2027 Spring or the 2027 Fall semester. These positions are full-time assignments appointed on a 3-year contract at the first instance and are renewable upon successful reappointment review. A tenure-track Assistant/Associate Professor is a full time, 10-month employee who teaches 24 credits per academic year. Tenure-track faculty normally teach 2 different courses with each section consisting typically of 25 students. Six credits of teaching release time will be provided to new faculty each year for the first three consecutive years of the appointment to support external research grant development and other significant research endeavors. Thereafter, release time may be available by application on competitive basis. A start-up grant (up to 80,000 RMB) will be provided to launch student-engaging research programs. Successful candidates will engage in high-quality teaching, impactful research, academic advising, student learning support, and service contributions to the university and the broader professional community. Tenure-track faculty must demonstrate a strong record of publication in reputable, peer-reviewed journals that are widely respected within the field. Teaching assignments and related responsibilities may include day, evening and weekend. Interest or experience in using advanced instructional technologies to improve the teaching/learning process is highly desirable. All faculty may be required to teach General Education courses as needed. Opportunities are also available to teach disciplinary support courses. Tenure-track candidates should possess a strong track record of publication and be ready to lead their research groups independently. Tenure-track candidates are expected to plan and conduct research and develop extramurally funded research programs involving students, which is essential for tenure and promotion. Tenure track candidates are also expected to publish peer-reviewed journal articles in impactful journals in Communication or closely related fields. In addition to teaching and student-engaging research duties, candidates are also expected to contribute to the growth of the programs, including but not limited to curriculum development, program assessment, student recruitment/advisement, senior project supervision, internship opportunities, research experiences for undergraduates (REU), etc. Qualifications: A Ph.D. in Communication Studies or related field is required; ABD can be considered with completion prior to the effective date of employment. English fluency is required. jobs.detailText: The University of St. Thomas (UST) announces a national search for the position of Dean of the Cameron School of Business, with employment to begin July 1, 2027. As UST works to increase enrollment and strengthen its standing as a major institution of higher education, we seek a Dean who will ensure the delivery of high-quality programs and instruction, foster mission-focused faculty development, and guide the strategic growth of the school while remaining faithful to the University's distinctive Catholic mission. UST prepares students for success in today's dynamic economy through a strong core curriculum in the liberal arts, exceptionally talented and dedicated faculty, and innovative co-curricular programs. An independent, coeducational private university, UST enrolls nearly 4,000 students (more than 3,000 undergraduates and almost 700 graduate students) from 34 states and 61 countries. We are Houston's only Catholic university, welcoming students of all faiths and backgrounds, and our student body reflects the city we serve. Houston is the nation's fourth-largest city and home to one of the most dynamic business environments in the world: a global center of energy, health care and life sciences, international trade, shipping and logistics, aerospace, and finance, with more than twenty Fortune 500 headquarters. The Cameron School of Business is located in the heart of this economy and is uniquely positioned to serve it. The Cameron School of Business offers undergraduate and graduate programs in business administration, management, marketing, accounting, finance, economics, and international business, including the Master of Business Administration (MBA) and a nationally recognized Master in Clinical Translation Management. The Dean's primary responsibility is stewardship of the school's academic performance and enrollment growth. The Dean will also serve as the school's principal ambassador to the Houston business community, cultivating partnerships with corporations, professional firms, entrepreneurs, alumni, and nonprofit organizations; ensuring that the school's programs and faculty scholarship respond to the needs of the region's employers; and maintaining the school's accreditations. The Dean reports directly to the Provost and serves as the chief academic and administrative officer of the Cameron School of Business. Stewardship and Strategic Role Functions Develop and lead a clear strategic vision for the Cameron School of Business, aligned with the University's strategic plan and Catholic mission, and integrate it into the school's academic planning and operations. Guide the strategic development, implementation, and evaluation of the school's academic programs to ensure their quality, relevance, and market competitiveness. Lead enrollment growth across the school, with particular emphasis on expanding the MBA program and other graduate offerings, by working closely with Enrollment Management and Marketing on recruitment strategy, program positioning, and yield. Ensure that the school's degree programs, concentrations, certificates, and executive education offerings are aligned with the workforce needs of the Houston and Gulf Coast business community, including energy, health care, finance, logistics, and technology, and lead the development of new programs where demand warrants. Foster the conditions and relationships that support creativity, innovation, and the formation of learning communities among faculty and students. Support faculty and staff professional development at both the individual and the departmental level. External Relations and Community Engagement Serve as the principal representative of the Cameron School of Business to the Houston business community, actively building and maintaining relationships with corporate executives, professional associations, chambers of commerce, and civic organizations. Lead a Dean's Business Advisory Council of regional executives to inform curriculum, provide internships and placement opportunities for students, and strengthen the school's reputation. Expand internship, mentorship, experiential learning, and career placement pipelines for students through employer partnerships. Work with Institutional Advancement to cultivate donors, secure gifts, endowed chairs, scholarships, and sponsored programs, and steward the school's benefactors and namesake legacy. Engage alumni as partners in recruitment, mentoring, philanthropy, and career placement. Support/Oversight Functions: Faculty and Department Chairs Recruit, develop, evaluate, and retain a high-quality faculty committed to teaching excellence, the University's mission, and the professional development of students. Develop and implement plans and allocate resources for faculty scholarship that addresses the needs of the region's business community and contributes to the school's AACSB standing. Encourage faculty engagement with industry through consulting, executive education, applied research partnerships, and service on corporate and civic boards. Create, implement, and evaluate the processes and procedures essential to an effective and collaborative academic enterprise, including faculty workload, evaluation, promotion, and tenure. Support/Oversight Functions: Academic Programs Collaborate with the other deans and with colleagues in Finance, Enrollment Management, Student Affairs, Institutional Advancement, Marketing, and Human Resources to develop and support programs that contribute to sustainable growth and high-quality learning outcomes. Oversee the selection, development, and orientation of department chairs. Facilitate the growth and enhancement of academic programs, both online and face-to-face, through support for sponsored research, grants, and partnerships. Oversee the school's assessment of student learning and the use of assessment results for continuous improvement. Ensure that curricula remain current with respect to technology, data analytics, and the evolving practices of the business professions. Academic Leadership Provide academic leadership within the school and across the University, and serve as a member of the Council of Deans. Ensure that academic program reports and proposals presented to the Provost meet appropriate quality standards to support effective review, decision-making, and implementation. Model and promote a culture of collegiality, shared governance, and accountability. Administrative and Regulatory Functions Direct the work

Send job Job Details About Wenzhou-Kean University Wenzhou-Kean University (WKU), located in Wenzhou, China, one of three Sino-American universities along with NYU Shanghai and Duke Kunshan University, is approved by the Ministry of Education of China. Launched in 2012, WKU offers a unique model of higher education in partnership with Kean University, a comprehensive, public university in the state of New Jersey that is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education. WKU sits on approximately 500 beautiful acres and currently enrolls about 5,500 undergraduate and graduate students, and it is now in the midst of a rapid growth that will bring enrollment to 7,000 students within the next three years. All instruction is in English, and all curriculum is provided by Kean University. In addition to its current 18 undergraduate programs, WKU has been approved by the Ministry of Education for offering 14 Master s and 3 doctorate programs including the M.A. in Communication. WKU highly values research-powered teaching and learning, and the average number of faculty publications and the Field-weighted Citation Impact are among the best of leading Chinese academic institutions. Wenzhou is one of the most vibrant and economically advanced developed cities on China s East Coast, located one hour by plane and three hours by high-speed train from Shanghai. Position: The College of Liberal Arts is seeking highly motivated individuals to join the Communication department at WKU. All faculty positions are full-time assignments, effective for the year of 2027 Spring or the 2027 Fall semester. These positions are full-time assignments appointed on a 3-year contract at the first instance and are renewable upon successful reappointment review. A Lecturer is a full-time, 10-month employee who teaches 30 credits per year. Or a Lecturer is a full-time, 11-month employee who teaches 39 credits per year. A lecturer provides student and learning support services during the assigned period. Lecturers will be expected to provide high quality teaching, student advisement, learning support services, and service to the university/college/school/program and/or professional community; and perform related work as required. Lecturer positions are non-tenure track. Teaching assignments and related responsibilities may include day, evening and weekend. Interest or experience in using advanced instructional technologies to improve the teaching/learning process is highly desirable. All faculty may be required to teach General Education courses as needed. Opportunities are also available to teach disciplinary support courses. Qualifications: A Ph.D. in Communication Studies or related field is required; ABD can be considered with completion prior to the effective date of employment. English fluency is required. Candidates should be able to teach a full range of undergraduate and postgraduate Communication courses related to Digital Media and Storytelling, including but not limited to: Media and Film Production, Digital Storytelling, AI, Communication and Digital Technology, Organisational Theory & Culture, Research Methods in Communication, and other upper level Communication electives. A minimum of two years of teaching experience in a college or university setting is preferred. Candidates with doctorate degrees from reputable universities (Carnegie R1 institutions or comparable research institutions with strong academic reputation in the fields) are encouraged to apply. Faculty positions at WKU offer: Annual salary is commensurate with qualifications and experience with the range from USD $60,000-$70,000 for Lecturer. Salary of extraordinary candidates shall be determined on a case-by-case basis. A well-rounded healthcare coverage, housing options and subsidy up to $3,000, home traveling up to $6,000 (2 international round-trip airfares), a reimbursement to cover relocation expenses up to $1,000 and shuttle bus to campus for work. WKU tuition waiver up to 50% for spouse/dependent children of faculty for undergraduate programs. The opportunity to teach high-quality students. About 50% of graduates have been admitted to graduate schools at the World s Top 50 Universities, and about 60% of graduates at the World s Top 100 Universities. Application Information: Applicants are REQUIRED to apply online . To receive full consideration by the search committee, candidates need to submit the following documents via Interfolio( https://apply.interfolio.com/195449 ). Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until positions are filled. Candidates should send cover letter, CV, statement of teaching philosophy, a research statement describing research interests, past accomplishments in research (such as 2-3 most representative peer-reviewed academic publications), and future research plans, unofficial transcripts, and the email contact information of three professional references, including references/names of potential referees from a current or recent direct supervisor. Three current letters of recommendation (within the last 3 months) will be required before advancement. Official transcripts for all degrees are required before appointment. Background Screening: Wenzhou-Kean University conducts background screenings on all candidates upon acceptance of a contingent offer and may use a third-party administrator to conduct background screenings. Send job Job Details Organization Job Details Description Adjuncts are hired on a course basis each term. Salary Range for Adjuncts teaching in this academic area is $300.00 - $4,500.00 per course. Governors State University’s College of Health and Human Services seeks to create an available pool of Adjunct Clinical and Teaching Faculty candidates to supervise graduate students and teach undergraduate and graduate courses in the Communication Disorders program. The major responsibilities of an adjunct faculty member would include one or more of the following:1. to serve as university supervisor of graduate students in external practica in speech-language pathology (i.e., serve as liaison between university and external practicum site); 2. to serve as a clinical supervisor of graduate students in a pre-practicum course in speech-language in pediatric and adult community settings; 3. to teach undergraduate and/or graduate courses in areas of need including child language, adult language, voice, and/or fluency. At Governors State University, adjunct faculty are hired as temporary faculty with teaching responsibilities for a specific course in a semester or summer session. Adjuncts are not a part of the faculty bargaining unit and are not included in membership of the Faculty Senate. Interested individuals are invited to complete a faculty profile and submit a cover letter that indicates the position/s applied for, a curriculum vitae, and transcripts for consideration. Required and Preferred Qualifications Minimum Qualifications - Master’s Degree in Speech-Language Pathology.-Certificate of Clinical Competence in Speech-Language Pathology (CCC-SLP).Preferred Qualifications -2 years of post-CFY clinical experience as an SLP-Experience supervising graduate students in clinical settings in speech-language pathology-Teaching experience. Supplemental Information Please attach the following documents to your application: Cover Letter CV or Resume Transcript Organization Working at Governors State University Success by Degrees GSU is an “island of excellence,” according to Dr. Martha J. Kanter, Under Secretary of the United States Department of Education. With bold, new initiatives, 23 bachelor’s, 27 master’s, and five doctoral degree programs, GSU excels at providing the quality education that is essential for success in today’s world. Success by Opportunity GSU’s exemplary efforts bring unequalled education opportunities to the region’s diverse population. The university is remarkably inclusive and serves students from a wide range of socio-economic and cultural backgrounds. The student body, like the faculty and staff, reflect a rich blend of ideas, perspectives, talents, and life experiences. Success by Innovation GSU, expanding on its commitment to excellence and reflecting the best research on student success, will become a full-service university with the admission of its inaugural freshman class in 2014. The groundbreaking Dual Degree Program encourages community college students to complete both an associate and bachelor’s degree at an affordable tuition rate and with comprehensive academic advising. Success by Commitment GSU is committed to serving as the region’s public square and making the community stronger through programs and partnerships in education, healthcare, government, and business. The Center for Performing Arts and Nathan Manilow Sculpture Park integrate arts and education. The university is also fully committed to sustainability through its alternative energy and conservation efforts. Success by Excellence GSU, the only public university in the Chicago Southland region, is a national model in providing education pathways that lead its graduates to lives rich in purpose, commitment, and contribution. jobs.detailText: The University of St.Gallen and its School of Management are inviting applications for an Associate Professorship / Assistant Professorship with Tenure Track (Open Rank) in Technology and Innovation Management. The triple accredited (EQUIS, AACSB, AMBA) university offers a stimulating and well-equipped research environment with a large network ranging from start-ups, small businesses to large firms to engage in research. The new professorship in the School of Management will become part of our dynamic faculty and will be invited to join the Institute of Technology Management (ITEM-HSG) and the Global Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation. We are seeking a colleague with proven expertise in one or more of the key domains of Technology and Innovation Management, including Global R&D, Innovation Strategy, Digital Innovation, Open Innovation, AI-driven Innovation, Technology Strategy, or related fields. Depending on qualifications, the appointment will be made at the level of Associate Professor or Assistant Professor with Tenure Track. The ideal candidate for the Associate Professorship has an internationally recognised and leading track record in research in leading journals in the field of Technology and Innovation Management, reflected in publications in top journals (e.g. FT50), a strong pipeline of promising research projects, a strong international academic network, ties with industry, and excellent teaching skills at all levels, including Executive Education. According to our claim "From insight to impact", the future colleague should convey scientific knowledge to students and have a significant impact on theory and practice. The successful candidate will also attract competitive external research funding (e.g. SNF, Innosuisse, ERC or industry collaborations), contribute actively to the academic community and governance of the University, and strengthen interdisciplinary collaboration across the School of Management and related technology-oriented disciplines. Associate Professors at the University of St.Gallen are provided with a budget to hire a doctoral student. The University of St.Gallen is committed to promoting equal opportunities and an inclusive working culture. We explicitly encourage women and members of underrepresented groups to apply. We offer dual-career and welcome services for newly appointed faculty (and their families). We seek to fill the position as of 1 August 2027 or by mutual agreement. For further information, please contact Professor Dr Björn Ambos, Dean of the School of Management and Chairman of the Appointment Committee ( [email protected] ). The application should include a cover letter, curriculum vitae, research and teaching statements (max. one page each), list of publications, teaching evaluations, two publications or working papers that best represent the applicant's current research, and contact information for two professional references that we may contact if shortlisted for the position. Candidates should submit their application to the President of the University of St.Gallen, Professor Dr Manuel Ammann, online via www.unisg.ch/professorships at the latest by 15 November 2026. Research talks are expected to take place on 20 January 2027.

Send job Job Details Assistant Professor, Tenure-Track Faculty Position in
Organizational Communication & Technology College/School/Unit: Moody College of Communication Department: Department of Communication Studies Posted: Jul 29, 2026 Apply By: Open until filled Description The Department of Communication Studies at the University of Texas
at Austin seeks applications for a full-time tenure-track assistant
professor faculty member in Organizational Communication and
Technology to begin Fall 2027. The Department of
Communication Studies is housed within the Moody College of Communication ,
which is ranked #1 in the QS World University rankings for
Communication and Media Studies among public universities in the
United States (and #4 among all universities globally) in 2026.
Moody College includes programs in Advertising and Public
Relations, Journalism and Media, Radio-Television-Film, and Speech,
Language, and Hearing Sciences. The Department of Communication Studies has strong graduate and
undergraduate programs and provides faculty research, teaching, and
leadership support/opportunities. At the graduate level, the
department is organized into three focal areas: Interpersonal
Communication; Rhetoric, Language, and Political Communication; and
Organizational Communication and Technology. The faculty are a
cohesive group that often collaborates on research with one
another, teaches a wide range of graduate and undergraduate
courses, and advises approximately 75 Ph.D. and M.A.
students. We welcome applications from scholars who study the intersection of
communication, organizing, organizations, and digital technologies,
including but not limited to AI. We invite applicants from a broad
range of theoretical orientations and methodological approaches,
including people with expertise in qualitative, quantitative, and
mixed methods. We are particularly interested in applicants whose
research advances our understanding of communication in
technology-rich organizational environments and complements the
work being done in the Organizational Communication and Technology
area. Research in that area currently examines topics such as
networks, remote and hybrid work, workplace cyberbullying, AI and
automation, human-AI collaboration, trust in AI and algorithmic
systems, digitization and digital media, crises and disasters,
hidden organizations, temporality, democratic organizing, team
dynamics, (in)visibility management, identity management, emergent
and informal organizing, work-life balance, resilience, and
wellbeing. Faculty have access to pre-and post-award external funding support
and have opportunities to join the vibrant research center and
institute culture in Moody College. We are especially interested in
candidates whose scholarship touches on social impact for the
public good, which could align with research units in Moody College
such as the Technology and Information Policy Institute, the Center
for Media Engagement, and the Center for Health Communication.
Additionally, UT Austin offers faculty opportunities to be involved
in interdisciplinary Grand Challenges such as Planet Texas 2050,
Good Systems (AI for Good), and Whole Communities-Whole

Joliet Junior College is an AA/EO employer and strongly encourages applications from candidates who would enhance the diversity of its staff. POSITION SUMMARY A Community Education Instructor is an instructor hired for an individual seminar for which he/she is qualified. The Community Education Instructor reports to one of the following coordinators (Community Education/Training/Contract Training) and provides quality instruction for the assigned courses. The instructor works with full-time staff in assessing students and following all course guidelines. Willingness to provide instructions at other campus sites is required. ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES AND KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 1. Provide instruction using appropriate technology, appropriate and effective standards of delivery, and a variety of methods of instruction. 2. To create a student-centered learning environment that is accessible to individual learners with diverse educational needs and goals. 3. Facilitate student learning by preparing, delivering, and assessing learning activities that are consistent with approved course outcomes. 4. Improve student learning by using a variety of teaching strategies. 5. Cultivate open-minded inquiry. 6. Encourage thoughtful, self-reflective assessment. 7. Promote cooperation and mutual respect among students. 8. Provide applicable and relevant classroom exercises. 9. Infuse multicultural and diverse perspectives into the instructional processes as appropriate, and conduct classes in a manner that demonstrates respect for individual and cultural differences. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS 1. One (1) year of experience in the subject matter. 2. Certification, licensure, endorsements and related experience will be considered. 3. Experience in instructional/classroom technology. 4. Demonstrated commitment to teaching and learning. 5. Ability to establish and maintain cooperative and effective working relationships with other members of the college and community, displaying cultural competence as well as emotional intelligence. 6. Demonstrated commitment to the college’s core values of respect and inclusion, sustainability, integrity, collaboration, humor and well-being, innovation, and quality. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 1. Associate’s Degree in Education, subject matter, or closely related field 2. Experience with traditional and non-traditional students from diverse backgrounds. 3. English and Spanish verbal and written communication proficiency. 4. Demonstrated multicultural competence. PHYSICAL DEMANDS 1. Normal classroom physical demands. WORKING CONDITIONS 1. Duties are performed indoors in the usual classroom and/or lab environment. A comprehensive community college, JJC also provides occupational education leading directly to employment, adult education and literacy programs, workforce development services, and student support services. Tucked in the middle of a wildlife preserve, bridging the banks of a lake and surrounded by its own Arboretum, Joliet Junior College is an educational community that embraces diversity and promotes personal growth. Each year, more than 35,000 students find the diverse, comprehensive high quality educational experience they are looking for at JJC. We hope that you will take a few minutes to explore the job opportunities we have available and consider becoming a part of this experience. The recruitment of qualified and diverse personnel is the cornerstone of JJC's commitment to an innovative, collaborative and inclusive educational community. At JJC, we respect the wealth of knowledge and experience each of our employees brings to the workplace. The College supports this commitment by providing personnel with excellent terms and conditions of employment, outstanding health and welfare benefits and programs for a secure retirement. JJC employees work in a wide variety of roles within the college, including faculty, support staff, and administrative positions. With such a diverse range of professions, JJC ensures that a wealth of development opportunities is available to employees. From personal growth, career advancement, and a dynamic and rewarding work atmosphere, employees have the resources they need to achieve a successful and fulfilling career at JJC. Joliet Junior College's open search procedures allow us to find the best available candidates for positions and to provide a balanced workforce to reflect the ethnic composition of the District we serve. statuses: Job description: The Department of Communication in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences at George Mason University seeks a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor of Communication, with a specialty in new/emerging communication technology and innovative research methods. Candidates should demonstrate an ability to teach graduate and undergraduate courses in a variety of areas, as listed above.

our students. Worcester State is centrally located in Massachusetts, about an

Island. Our 58-acre campus is nestled in the residential northwest
side of Worcester--the second largest city in New England and home
to 37,000 college students at more than a dozen colleges and
universities. Over 6,000 of those students attend Worcester
State--approximately 5,300 are undergraduates and 1,000 are
graduate students. Learn more about us at worcester.edu/about . Job Description: About the Program: The Communication program provides students with a broad liberal
arts foundation while developing critical thinking, communication,
media literacy, and professional skills. Through the study of
journalism, media systems, digital communication, and public
discourse, students learn to critically evaluate media institutions
and participate meaningfully in civic and community life. The
program values the role of independent, local, and community media
in fostering democratic participation, public dialogue, and
informed citizenship. Job Description: The Department of Communication at Worcester State University
invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor
position in Journalism and Media Studies beginning in the Fall
Semester of 2027. We seek a dynamic teacher-scholar committed to
undergraduate liberal arts education who can contribute to a
diverse and interdisciplinary Communication program that emphasizes
critical inquiry, media literacy, civic engagement, and practical
communication skills. The successful candidate will teach foundational and advanced
courses in journalism, media studies, and communication while
helping students understand the vital role that independent, local,
and community-based media play in democratic societies. Areas of
teaching may include any of the following areas: news writing and
reporting, digital journalism, media ethics, media literacy,
community media, independent media, alternative media, media and
democracy, and related subjects. The candidate should be able to
integrate both theoretical and applied approaches to communication,
preparing students to critically analyze contemporary media systems
while developing practical skills in reporting, content creation,
and digital communication. For a small liberal arts institution that values close
faculty-student engagement, the successful candidate will
demonstrate a commitment to student-centered teaching, mentorship,
and experiential learning. Opportunities may include supervising
student media organizations, advising student publications,
fostering partnerships with local media organizations, and
supporting community-engaged learning initiatives. In addition to teaching, the appointee will be expected to maintain
an active scholarly and/or creative agenda, engage in curriculum
development, advise undergraduate students, and participate in
departmental, university, and/or community service. We are
particularly interested in candidates whose work examines
journalism's public service mission, the challenges and
opportunities facing independent and community media, media equity
and representation, digital journalism, media policy, civic
communication, or related areas. General Statement of Duties: Teach undergraduate courses in journalism, media studies, and
communication. Develop and teach courses in areas such as journalism,
community media, independent media, media literacy, media ethics,
and multimedia communication. Contribute to core Communication curriculum requirements. Advise and mentor undergraduate students. Participate in curriculum development and assessment
activities. Maintain an active program of scholarship, creative activity,
or professional engagement. Engage in departmental, university, and community service. Support experiential learning opportunities, including student
media production, internships, and community partnerships. Requirements: Required Qualifications: Ph.D., in Communication, Journalism, Media Studies, Mass
Communication, or a closely related field by September 1,
2027. Candidates should demonstrate evidence of effective

jobs.detailText: About ZIBS Rooted in China with a global vision, Zhejiang University International Business School (ZIBS) uphold s its "5i" philos ophy— International, Interdisciplinary, Innovative, Inclusive and Integrative. The School promotes exchange and mutual understanding across global business communities, facilitates the deep integration of technological innovation and industry, and strives to nurture top‑tier interdisciplinary innovators equipped with global leadership capabilities. ZIBS pursues targeted, distinctive development in emerging interdisciplinary areas including Sci‑Tech Finance, Digital Intelligence Management, and International Business and Globalization. Adhering to a strategy of selectivity, excellence and specialization, ZIBS has built high‑level research platforms. Drawing on these resources, the school aims to develop a global‑minded international business education model centered on science and technology. Preferred Research Areas Corporate Finance, FinTech, Quantitative Finance, Digital Accounting, Digital Marketing, Information Systems and Business Analytics, International Business, Organizations and Strategy in the Digital Age, as well as related areas. Positions Full Professor: Well‑known scholars, academicians and highly‑cited researchers in their respective fields, with extensive teaching and research experience and the capacity to lead disciplinary development. Associate Professor (Tenured or Tenure-Track): Assistant professor or above at world renowned universities, strong candidates of national young talent programs. Demonstrate strong academic influence, with the ability of leading high-quality research projects. Assistant Professor (Tenure-Track): Young talents with demonstrated academic potential and competitiveness for national‑level young talent programs, with an outstanding publication record or strong potential to publish in top‑tier journals. Haina Scholar (Teaching-Track) : This full-time teaching-track position is primarily open to Non-Chinese candidates. Applicants should possess a solid theoretical foundation and professional expertise, with the ability to conduct high-quality research and teaching. A doctoral degree from a reputable university worldwide and at least two years of research and teaching experience are generally required. Postdoctoral Fellow PhD graduates from world-renowned universities with strong potential for excellent research and teaching performance. Work and Living Conditions 1. Academic environment: Drawing on Zhejiang University’s premier academic standing, the school provides an open, inclusive research climate and world‑class international educational resources, nurtured by a collegial and diverse international faculty body. 2. Career Development: Independent PI role with doctoral supervision privileges (available to tenure-track and tenured faculty); Well-defined career progression with annual reviews; access to professional development training. 3. Research support: Start-up fund will be commensurate in line with qualifications, plus strong support for allocation of doctor/master students and postdoctoral recruitment quota. A bilingual campus with international efficient administrative and service structure. 4. Remuneration and benefits: Competitive remuneration commensurate with qualifications and experience. 5. Housing arrangement: Rental of a fully furnished apartment (available to all faculty); purchase of an on-campus Hainashire apartment (available for tenure-track and tenured positions). 6. Other support: Enrollment of children in preferred local schools; Assist in permanent residence permit application for foreign faculty; Fine medical services provided by the two branch sections of the affiliated hospitals of ZJU in the neighborhood, etc. Application All applicants shall provide the following application materials (in PDF format) to [email protected] , with the subject titled “Name - Position Applied For”. Please also specify in application email the source platform through which you learned about this vacancy. 1. A detailed CV (please include your current email address, attached with a recent color ID photo or provide the photo separately); 2. A cover letter; 3. A research statement; 4. A teaching statement; 5. Three recommendation letters; 6. Three representative publications or other innovative research achievements (for papers accepted or in the R&R stage ， please provide supporting documents) ； 7. Identification documents (non-Mainland China residents can provide passports or other identification documents); 8. Educational and degree certificates; * To receive full consideration, applications should be received online by November 10, 2026, but the search will remain open until filled. Qualified applicants will usually receive an email notification within 1–2 weeks after submission; otherwise, it will be assumed that they did not pass the initial screening. jobs.detailText: Position Description NYU Shanghai is currently inviting applications for a faculty position in Management and Organizations at all ranks. For further details about the research centers and institutes at NYU Shanghai, please visit this webpage: https://research.shanghai.nyu.edu/. Terms of employment at NYU Shanghai are comparable to NYU New York and other U.S. institutions with respect to research start-up funds and compensation, and they include housing subsidies and educational subsidies for children. Faculty may in certain cases have the opportunity to spend time at NYU New York and other sites of the NYU Global Network, engaging in both research and teaching. Qualifications We seek candidates who have completed a Ph.D. in Management and Organizations or a closely related discipline. We invite applications from candidates in any field and have a special interest in those with expertise in Organizational Theory, Strategy, and Entrepreneurship. Application Instructions Applicants should submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, statement of research, statement of teaching interests, and at least one writing sample (e.g., job market paper) via Interfolio. Additionally, applicants (applying at the Assistant or Associate without tenure ranks) will be prompted to enter the names and email addresses of at least three evaluators. Each referee will be contacted to upload a confidential letter of recommendation through Interfolio. Applications may be received until October 31st, 2026. Review of applications will begin on October 15th, 2026 and will continue until the position is filled. To apply, follow this link: https://apply.interfolio.com/194865. If you have any questions, please email the NYU Shanghai NY Office of Faculty Recruitment: [email protected] . About NYU Shanghai NYU Shanghai is the third degree-granting campus within New York University’s Global Network. It is the first higher education joint venture in China authorized to grant degrees that are accredited in the U.S. as well as in China. All teaching is conducted in English. A research university with liberal arts and science at its core, NYU Shanghai resides in one of the world's great cities with a vibrant intellectual community. NYU Shanghai recruits scholars of the highest caliber who are committed to NYU's global vision of transformative teaching and innovative research and who embody the global society in which we live. NYU’s Global Network includes degree-granting campuses in New York, Shanghai, and Abu Dhabi, complemented by thirteen additional academic centers across the world. Faculty and students may circulate within the Network in pursuit of common research interests and cross-cultural, interdisciplinary endeavors, both local and global. For people in the EU, click here for information on your privacy rights under GDPR: www.nyu.edu/it/gdpr. NYU Shanghai is an equal opportunity employer and strongly encourages applications from all interested persons. NYU Shanghai affirms the value of differing perspectives on the world as we strive to build the strongest possible university with the widest reach.

Send job Job Details The Texas A&M University College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts (PVFA) invites applications for a full-time, nine-month tenure-track or a tenured faculty position in Interactive Media and Creative Technology at the rank of Assistant Professor or Associate Professor. Rank and tenure status will be commensurate with the candidate’s academic and professional experience and qualifications. The anticipated start date is August 1, 2027. The College and the Technical Arts & Interactive Media (TAIM) Section in the Visualization Program seek an innovative scholar, artist, designer, and educator whose research and creative practice advance the evolving fields of interactive art and design, computational media, and interdisciplinary creative technologies. We are particularly interested in candidates whose work investigates how emerging technologies can expand creative expression, human experience, and design innovation through artistic inquiry, experimentation, critical engagement, and technological exploration. The successful candidate will join a vibrant interdisciplinary environment that bridges art, design, computation, science, and technology. They will be expected to establish and sustain a nationally and internationally recognized program of scholarly and/or creative research and contribute to teaching and mentorship across the Visualization Program’s undergraduate, master’s, and PhD programs. We value collaborative and forward-looking research and creative practices that address contemporary opportunities and challenges through innovative approaches to interactive systems, creative computation, emerging media, and human-centered technologies. Candidates should demonstrate the potential for, or an established record of, scholarly and creative excellence and the capacity to develop a significant and visible research and/or creative practice appropriate to their career stage. We especially welcome work that integrates artistic practice, design research, computational approaches, and technological innovation through interdisciplinary methods. Areas of expertise may include, but are not limited to: · Interactive Art and Design · Creative Technologies · Computational Media and Creative Coding · Immersive and Spatial Media (AR/VR/MR/XR) · Human-Computer Interaction and Human-AI Interaction Design · Artificial Intelligence and Creative Practice · Physical Computing and Responsive Environments · Generative and Procedural Art · Computational Storytelling and Interactive Narrative · Media Arts and Experimental Interfaces · Digital Performance and Performative Technologies · Other emerging interdisciplinary areas at the intersection of art, design, computation, science, and technology The ideal candidate will demonstrate a commitment to interdisciplinary research, creative practice, teaching, and mentorship and will contribute to the Technical Arts & Interactive Media Section’s mission of integrating artistic creativity, scientific inquiry, design thinking, and technological innovation. Through research, creative activity, teaching, and collaboration, the successful candidate will help shape new directions for visual and interactive experiences and contribute to the continued development of the Visualization Program’s undergraduate and graduate educational and research initiatives. About the College The College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts is a new college within the Texas A&M University System, with a diverse and dynamic mission, 109 faculty, over 15 staff members, and projected exponential growth over the next five years. The college was formed from three departments and programs across the university: the Department of Visualization, the Department of Performance Studies, and the Dance Science Program. The mission of PVFA places a heavy emphasis on faculty and student collaboration and interdisciplinary work in both scholarly and creative research. Texas A&M University leadership has charged the college with developing innovative research and creative works, public performances, and degree offerings at the undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral levels that build on our strength in merging art and science, alongside the traditional fields of music, dance, art, and theater. Faculty also have access to a virtual production stage through the Virtual Production Institute. Applicants should consult the college's website to review our academic and research programs (https://pvfa.tamu.edu/). Some examples of (but not limited to) the types of scholarship that would fit the call include : Social, political and/or cultural implications for media of artificial intelligence Critical approaches to media and data infrastructures, platforms, and algorithms Creator economies (advocacy, activism, professionalization, uneven access) Political economy of emerging media Cultural policies and legislation (regulation, ethical issues, and intellectual property) Intersection of media industries with environmental issues and vulnerable populations Geopolitics and global media corporations Changes in social media, streaming, and/or immersive platforms Evolutions in the news industry and journalistic practices Media industries and audiences Media production hubs and urban transformations Promotion, media strategy, and social change Media labor dynamics We are especially interested in scholars who study media industries in relation to power and inequality, particularly in the context of, but not limited to, gender/queer/disability studies. Job Responsibilities Responsibilities of tenured faculty members include undergraduate and graduate teaching assignments, an active program of research in the candidate’s area of scholarly expertise, and service contributions in accordance with the university policy for tenured appointments. We are seeking someone with leadership experience and/or interest in eventual departmental leadership. Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey, is among America’s highest-ranked, most diverse public research universities and is the oldest, largest, and top-ranked public university in the New York/New Jersey metropolitan area. Established in 1766 and the state’s land-grant institution, Rutgers is home to more than 71,000 students and 27,300 full- and part-time faculty and staff who learn, work, and serve the public at three main Rutgers campuses across New Jersey and at locations around the region. With 29 schools and colleges, over 550 degree programs, over 610,000 alumni, and thousands of professional and personal enrichment continuing education programs, Rutgers’ impact is felt around the world. SC&I has more than 2,500 matriculating students and teaches thousands of other Rutgers students in our five undergraduate programs, two masters degrees, interdisciplinary doctoral program, and non-degree continuing education programs. We value our culture of collegiality and we work hard to support the success of our full- and part-time faculty, staff, and students. For more about the school and its activities, see: http://comminfo.rutgers.edu. Faculty in the Department of Journalism and Media Studies have doctoral and professional degrees in a variety of fields, including communication, journalism, law, sociology, history, anthropology and other areas. We study and practice the operation of media at local, national, and international levels, and our research methods range from humanistic to social scientific. This year marks the 100-year anniversary of journalism education at Rutgers. successful college teaching and who share our commitment to
professional preparation within the context of an interdisciplinary
and immersive liberal arts education. A wide variety of specialties
will be considered including, but not limited to, strategic
planning, account management, event/experiential marketing, art
direction/graphic design, and audience/media research. Ithaca College is committed to building a diverse academic
community and encourages members of underrepresented groups to
apply. Experience that contributes to the diversity of the college
is appreciated. Application Instructions: Interested applicants must apply online
at ithaca.edu/jobs and attach a resume and cover letter. Questions
about online applications should be directed to the Office of Human
Resources at (607) 274-8000. All bargaining unit faculty members shall be covered by the
collective bargaining agreement between Ithaca College and Services
Employees International Union, Local 200 United. Part-time or
adjunct bargaining unit employees are all part-time faculty
employed by Ithaca College at its Ithaca, New York campus including
but not limited to faculty in the titles of Lecturer or
Adjunct. Visa sponsorship is not provided for this position. Hiring rate: $2,059.25 per credit hour. In an effort to promote campus safety and the security of College
resources, Ithaca College will, consistent with the requirements of
the law and prudent practices, conduct criminal background
investigations per College policy. This position is subject to a
criminal background check. All offers of employment are contingent
upon review of the criminal background check. Company Ithaca College is a private residential campus where students find life-changing academic pathways, powerful career networks, and lifelong community. Founded by a homesick violinist with a big vision, Ithaca College started out as the Ithaca Conservatory of Music — combining theory, practice, and performance from its inception . By the 1920s, academic programs expanded to include business, speech therapy, physical education, and the dramatic arts. IC was originally located in downtown Ithaca and moved to the present campus on South Hill overlooking Cayuga Lake in the 1960s. Situated near 150 majestic waterfalls in the Finger Lakes region of New York State, the city of Ithaca, New York, has been ranked as the best college town in the United States — hosting tech startups, a “killer music scene,” Broadway-caliber theatre, and world-class restaurants as well as alumni-owned ice cream shops. Ithaca College offers more than 140 majors and minors through its five schools. Whether our alumni are winning Pulitzers, launching nonprofits, anchoring broadcast news, leading multibillion-dollar companies, or revolutionizing patient care (among many other pursuits and accomplishments), students at Ithaca College learn different and leave different. Join an innovative educational community, where faculty and staff learn, thrive, and collaborate. IC will make you ready to take your career to new heights, giving you the chance to create your own path to success while you contribute to growing the minds of future generations. As an employee at Ithaca College, you’ll get much more than a competitive salary and the traditional advantages . We pride ourselves on providing our employees with the most comprehensive benefits possible. Beyond benefits, you’ll enjoy the kind of uniquely rewarding work environment that can only be found in a vibrant college community. We encourage and contribute to the personal and professional development of our faculty and staff. We understand that it’s the people who work here that make Ithaca College special, and we strive to be an employer of choice in our region. jobs.detailText: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor – Leading People and Organizations Gabelli School of Business, Fordham University The Leading People and Organizations (LPO) Area at the Gabelli School of Business invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor, beginning Fall 2027. We welcome applicants whose research addresses questions at the intersection of organizations and society, with particular interest in the following areas: organizational theory and design, sustainability and social impact, entrepreneurship and innovation, and the management of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. Candidates whose work engages questions of purpose, responsibility, and human flourishing in organizational life are especially encouraged to apply. The LPO Area is built around a conviction that management scholarship should advance human dignity and well-being — not merely organizational efficiency. Our faculty study how individuals, teams, and organizations can be forces for good: through ethical leadership, trustworthy institutions, social innovation, and sustainable enterprise. The LPO Area is home to the Center for Humanistic Management and Fordham's sustainable business, management, and entrepreneurship programs, including the Fordham Foundry. Faculty engage with both scholarly communities and the broader New York City business ecosystem across Fordham's Lincoln Center and Rose Hill campuses. The ideal candidate must possess a Ph.D. in Management, Organizational Behavior, or a related field from an accredited institution (expected completion no later than July 1, 2027, is acceptable). Candidates must demonstrate strong research potential and commitment to excellence in graduate and undergraduate teaching. We are a collaborative area that values intellectual generosity, and we seek colleagues who thrive in an environment of mutual support and shared purpose. Applications should include a cover letter providing a research statement and description of teaching interests, a curriculum vitae, three letters of reference, and an example of scholarly work. All materials should be submitted via Interfolio at Apply - Interfolio by September 1, 2026 . Candidates are encouraged to apply early, as interview decisions may be made before the deadline. Questions may be directed to Randy Krevat at [email protected] . Fordham University is an independent Catholic university in the Jesuit tradition. Fordham's Jesuit mission emphasizes ethical leadership, social responsibility, and engagement with the broader public good, values that animate the LPO faculty's teaching and scholarship. Fordham's Gabelli School of Business is guided by the principle of "Business with Purpose" — preparing leaders who generate not only profit, but wide-ranging benefits for society. The Gabelli School of Business is AACSB-accredited. Fordham is an Equal Opportunity Employer and welcomes applications from candidates of all backgrounds.

The college first opened its doors to students in 1968 after Henderson Hall, the first building on campus, was completed. The first class consisted of 592 full-time and 703 part-time students. Included among its distinctions, CCM was the first community college in New Jersey to be named a National Center of Academic Excellence in Cyber Defense Education by the National Security Agency and Department of Homeland Security. jobs.detailText: Call for Applications At the University of St.Gallen, Switzerland, researchers from different disciplines and generations convene at St.Gallen Collegium. Fellows pursue their own research and a joint project focusing on a theme related to one of the Grand Challenges of our time. For the third Collegium year 2027/2028 (September 1, 2027-May 31, 2028), St.Gallen Collegium will award fellowships to scholars whose work addresses the theme: "Performance: The What, How, and Why of Optimization" About the Theme The call for “more performance” has returned with force across European business and politics as a reaction to perceived decreasing productivity of many economies. It simultaneously reflects changing values and preferences of their societies as to what, how, and why shall be optimized. Companies announce this openly: Nestlé declares it wants to be more performance-driven; UBS insists that performance must again be at the center. Politics has followed suit. The Schweizerischer Arbeitgeberverband warns of a spreading culture of Lifestyle Freizeit. The German CDU campaigns on Leistung muss sich wieder lohnen — performance must pay. Commentators demand “work instead of woke.” The word does considerable heavy lifting. The concept itself is rarely examined. Performance, as we use it today, has a relatively recent history. The historian Nina Verheyen has argued that measurable, comparable individual performance took its current shape in the nineteenth century, shaped by the rise of mass schooling, industrial labor, and the welfare state. Earlier traditions tied performance more closely to the work itself — to craft, to care, to standards of excellence carried out within a practice and judged by its own internal norms. The shift towards abstracted, quantified output was not inevitable. It was constructed, and it can be interrogated. Much of what gets called individual performance has irreducibly relational features. Contributions emerge between people, in context, supported by predecessors, colleagues, institutions, and inherited knowledge. Measurement systems do not simply reflect performance — they constitute what counts as performance and render other kinds of contribution invisible. The colleague who unblocks others, the institutional memory carried by long-serving staff, the care work that makes everything else possible: these tend to fall outside what is captured and rewarded. The map is not the territory, but in performance cultures, the map increasingly determines whose work counts. The language of performance also carries significant moral weight. A meritocratic reading treats outcomes as broadly deserved and shortfalls as broadly personal. Harvard moral philosopher Michael Sandel has argued that this framing generates hubris among those who succeed and humiliation among those who do not — with consequences for social solidarity that extend well beyond the individuals concerned. Whether and how strongly this dynamic operates across different institutional and cultural settings is itself a pressing research question, one that has gained new urgency in recent debates on polarization, resentment, and the fraying of social cohesion. The performance of an economy is also shaped by forces no individual or firm controls. Demographic change is perhaps the most consequential of these. What does prosperity mean if, by 2050, approximately 30% of the Swiss population is over 65, compared to just 9% in 1950? What does it mean for productivity, innovation, and care if Germany's population begins to shrink and declines by an estimated 13% by mid-century? How can societies harness the potential of longer lives rather than treating extended longevity solely as a fiscal burden? These questions demand that we rethink how and what counts as economic performance — and for whom. The question of who defines what counts as performance, and who benefits from the categories thereby created, is partly political and philosophical, not only technical. St.Gallen Collegium invites researchers from all fields who are interested in a solution-oriented, interdisciplinary discourse on performance. Possible avenues of research include: – The history and genealogy of performance: How did measurable, individual performance become the dominant frame for assessing human contribution? How does this relate to our freedom and sovereignty as individuals and as institutions? What was lost and what was gained in that transition? What alternative traditions — of craft, vocation, care, or collective achievement — might inform different approaches today? – Performance as a legal standard: The law’s measure of capacity and the limits of what can be demanded. Across legal domains, performance is not only observed and rewarded but normatively constructed: the law determines what can reasonably be expected of individuals — and where that expectation must stop. Tax law assesses citizens by their ability to pay (wirtschaftliche Leistungsfähigkeit), choosing proxies — income, wealth, consumption — for a capacity it cannot directly observe; social insurance law mirrors this by defining incapacity and the residual capacity one must still use; employment law fixes a standard of diligent performance owed under contract. How do constitutions and legislatures turn the diffuse idea of performance or potential performance into operable legal measures? – Measurement and its limits: What do performance metrics actually capture, and what do they systematically miss? How do measurement systems shape behavior, institutions, and the distribution of recognition and reward? How can organizations design evaluation systems that are both rigorous and honest about their limitations? How does the dominating institutional logic influence our conception of performance? – Relational and collective dimensions of performance: How do individual contributions depend on and emerge from collaborative structures, shared knowledge, social norms, and institutional context? How can organizations, firms, and states better recognize and sustain the forms of work that enable others to perform? – Performance, merit, and social cohesion: How does meritocratic ideology shape attitudes towards inequality, solidarity, and belonging? What are the psychological and political consequences of cultures that attribute success and failure primarily to individual effort? How do these dynamics differ across class, gender, migration background, and generation? – Demographic change a
