that is consistently recognized as one of the top comprehensive
colleges in the nation. Founded in 1855 as the New Jersey State
Normal School, TCNJ maintains the eighth highest four-year
graduation rate among all public colleges and universities. It is
ranked by Money as one of the top 15 public colleges “most likely
to pay off financially,” and U.S. News & World Report rates it
the No. 1 public institution among regional universities in the
northeast. Position Overview The Department of Communication, Journalism, and Film (CJF) at The
College of New Jersey (TCNJ) invites applications for a
tenure-track Assistant Professor position in technology-mediated
interpersonal communication. We seek an outstanding teacher-scholar
whose research and teaching expertise centers on the intersection
of interpersonal or relational communication and
technology-mediated communication. The successful candidate's research program should keep
interpersonal or relational communication at its core, even as it
engages with technology. Examples of research programs that align
with this position include how technology-mediated communication
shapes identity and/or personal and relational well-being; how
communication processes such as conflict management,
self-disclosure, and social support unfold through
technology-mediated channels; and how technology-mediated
communication is used within, or influences, couples and families.
Research centered on digital media, mass communication, or
technology in society that does not also engage relational or
interpersonal communication falls outside the scope of this
search. Consistent with TCNJ's teacher-scholar model, the successful
candidate will teach undergraduate courses including Introduction
to Communication Theory, Interpersonal Communication, and Research
Methods, along with technology-mediated interpersonal communication
courses that reflect their research expertise, while developing
curriculum that bridges theory and practice. They will also mentor
undergraduate students in professional development and research. In
their research role, the faculty member will conduct original
research in technology-mediated interpersonal communication,
publish in peer-reviewed journals and other appropriate venues,
present at professional conferences, and collaborate with
departmental colleagues. Service expectations include participating
in departmental, school, and college-level service, contributing to
professional organizations and the broader academic community, and
engaging in community outreach as appropriate. About the Department of Communication, Journalism, and
Film The Department of Communication, Journalism, and Film (CJF) is one
of the four departments within TCNJ's School of the Arts and
Communication. The department offers three majors: Communication
Studies, Film and Television, and Journalism and Professional
Writing, serving over 250 major students. There are four
specializations in the Communication Studies major: Emerging
Communication Technologies, Health Communication, Interpersonal and
Strategic Communication, and Mass Media and Social Media. Aligned
with the School's mission, CJF cultivates analytical, critical, and
creative thinking while fostering conscientious global citizenship
and lifelong learning. Through integrated teaching and scholarship,
we prepare students to make meaningful contributions to their
communities and chosen careers. Our departmental mission centers on
maximizing student engagement in the discovery and creation of
knowledge, art, and information. We encourage independent
initiative and inquiry while instilling a passion for lifelong
learning. Our faculty serve as active professional scholars and
writers who significantly advance knowledge and understanding in
their respective fields. Additionally, CJF faculty prepare students
to engage thoughtfully with a range of perspectives, experiences,
and communities, equipping them with the knowledge and skills
necessary to serve and strengthen the communities in which they
will live and work. For more information about the departments, please visit https://cjf.tcnj.edu/ . Qualifications Required: Have a Ph.D. in Communication Studies or a closely related
field by the time of appointment. ABD candidates will be considered
but must complete all degree requirements before starting the
position. Demonstrate expertise in technology-mediated interpersonal or
relational communication research. Show evidence of scholarly potential through publications,
conference presentations, or dissertation research. Demonstrate knowledge of and commitment to best teaching
practices. Demonstrate cultural competency and ability to foster inclusive
learning environments and mutual respect for students and

agenda complements and extends current faculty strengths within the

jobs.detailText: SMU Presidential Early Career Professorship - (2600006E) Description Join Singapore Management University As A Presidential Early Career Professor Tenure-Track Assistant Or Associate Professor Positions Singapore Management University (SMU), a research-intensive university with recognised strengths in management, computing, law, economics, and social sciences, invites outstanding scholars to join us as tenure-track Assistant Professor or Associate Professor under the University's Presidential Early Career Professorship (SMU-PEP) Scheme . Following the successful inaugural round of the SMU-PEP Scheme in 2025, SMU is pleased to open its second call for applications from scholars whose research aligns with SMU’s strategic research priorities: Digital Transformation Sustainable Living Growth in Asia Early-career scholars from any academic discipline whose work addresses the challenges of ageing societies, sustainable cities, or resilient workforces are especially encouraged to apply. Exceptional candidates working outside these priority areas are welcome to apply. What We Offer Successful candidates will be appointed to a named (early-career) professorship and can expect: A vibrant and collegial research and teaching environment Internationally competitive compensation A generous sign-on bonus and start-up research grant Comprehensive benefits The opportunity to live and work in one of Asia’s most exciting and cosmopolitan cities Qualifications Applicants should: Hold a Ph.D. or equivalent degree, earned within six years of the application date Have postdoctoral research and teaching experience Demonstrate an excellent research track record, particularly in interdisciplinary work Show strong potential to contribute high-impact future research Application Instructions Please submit the following by 31 October 2026 : Cover letter with your research and teaching statements Curriculum vitae Three research samples Evidence of teaching effectiveness Shortlisted candidates will be notified and asked to arrange for three academic reference letters. The expected start date is 1 July 2027 , or as mutually agreed. All applications will be handled in strict confidence. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. At SMU, we value diversity and are committed to building an inclusive and supportive workplace for all.

jobs.detailText: « A place where knowledge is created » – As a leading business university we set global standards for research and teaching by promoting integrative thought, responsible action and an entrepreneurial spirit of innovation in business and society. Associate Professorship / Assistant Professorship with Tenure Track (Open Rank) in Technology and Innovation Management The University of St.Gallen and its School of Management are inviting applications for an Associate Professorship / Assistant Professorship with Tenure Track (Open Rank) in Technology and Innovation Management. The triple accredited (EQUIS, AACSB, AMBA) university offers a stimulating and well-equipped research environment with a large network ranging from start-ups, small businesses to large firms to engage in research. The new professorship in the School of Management will become part of our dynamic faculty and will be invited to join the Institute of Technology Management (ITEM-HSG) and the Global Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation. We are seeking a colleague with proven expertise in one or more of the key domains of Technology and Innovation Management, including Global R&D, Innovation Strategy, Digital Innovation, Open Innovation, AI-driven Innovation, Technology Strategy, or related fields. Depending on qualifications, the appointment will be made at the level of Associate Professor or Assistant Professor with Tenure Track. The ideal candidate for the Associate Professorship has an internationally recognised and leading track record in research in leading journals in the field of Technology and Innovation Management, reflected in publications in top journals (e.g. FT50), a strong pipeline of promising research projects, a strong international academic network, ties with industry, and excellent teaching skills at all levels, including Executive Education. According to our claim "From insight to impact", the future colleague should convey scientific knowledge to students and have a significant impact on theory and practice. The successful candidate will also attract competitive external research funding (e.g. SNF, Innosuisse, ERC or industry collaborations), contribute actively to the academic community and governance of the University, and strengthen interdisciplinary collaboration across the School of Management and related technology-oriented disciplines. Associate Professors at the University of St.Gallen are provided with a budget to hire a doctoral student. The University of St.Gallen is committed to promoting equal opportunities and an inclusive working culture. We explicitly encourage women and members of underrepresented groups to apply. We offer dual-career and welcome services for newly appointed faculty (and their families). We seek to fill the position as of 1 August 2027 or by mutual agreement. For further information, please contact Professor Dr Bj ö rn Ambos, Dean of the School of Management and Chairman of the Appointment Committee ( [email protected] ). The application should include a cover letter, curriculum vitae, research and teaching statements (max. one page each), list of publications, teaching evaluations, two publications or working papers that best represent the applicant's current research, and contact information for two professional references that we may contact if shortlisted for the position. Candidates should submit their application to the President of the University of St.Gallen, Professor Dr Manuel Ammann, online via www.unisg.ch/professorships at the latest by 15 November 2026. Research talks are expected to take place on 20 January 2027.

Send job Job Details Organization Job Details Associate/ Full Professor of Interactive Media Film and Media Arts, School of Communication, American University The School of Communication at American University (AU) in Washington, D.C., invites applications for a full-time, faculty position at the rank of associate or full professor, with an emphasis on interactive storytelling, worldbuilding, and/or playful design in the public interest. Depending on qualifications, the appointee may be recommended for tenure at the time of hiring. Candidates should hold a terminal degree as appropriate to their focus, such as an MFA or Ph.D. The salary range is from $105,000- $124,000. The School of Communication (SOC) at American University engages the most pressing issues of our time through teaching, scholarship, and professional experiences in communication and media. In the Film and Media Arts division, our faculty and students make media that matters in and beyond one of the most dynamic and influential cities in the world. The candidate is expected to work closely with or lead American University’s Game & Interactive Media Center, which is a world-class hub for experiential education, interactive storytelling, and computational media with a public purpose. While the Center is increasingly focused on undergraduate learning, its graduate programs were ranked #24 in the world by the Princeton Review in 2026, including the MA in Game Design and the MFA in Games and Interactive Media. The Center recently launched a new minor in Game Design, with one track for media studies students and another for those with an interest in computer science and game development. The ideal candidate will be an outstanding media maker, educator, and curricular strategist. They should ideally be comfortable with many principles of good game design. The candidate’s practice in interactive media should connect to one or more domains in the public interest: the environment, health, urban and spatial planning, education, or social issue storytelling, and should interface with science communication and journalism, museums, nonprofits, etc. As more AI tools are integrated into production pipelines, the candidate should have some knowledge of where such tools are useful and how they can be guided, and be able to engage thoughtfully with students who are both AI resistant and AI enthusiasts. Job responsibilities may include teaching courses; directing undergraduate and graduate game programs; mentoring students; securing new partnerships and funding for original media projects and high-impact collaborations; and participating in School of Communication and University governance. The position, which will begin in August of 2027, comes with powerful opportunities for collaboration with a tremendous mix of organizations in Washington, DC, from arts funders to policy think tanks to global nonprofits. Collaborating across the university with our world-class faculty is particularly well-suited to the Game & Interactive Media Center and is encouraged. Consideration of applications will commence on November 1, 2026. Candidate interviews will begin in late 2026/early 2027 and continue until the position is filled. To apply, submit a letter of application, curriculum vitae, one letter of recommendation (two more letters will be requested for those who reach the interview stage), a teaching portfolio, optional creative portfolio, and optional excerpt of exemplary publications; finalist candidates will be asked for two letters of recommendation (likely to coincide with interviews). Please submit applications via Workday. Please contact the SOC Faculty Affairs Coordinator at 202-885-2133 or email facultyaffairs_SOC@american.edu if you have any questions. For more about the School of Communication, please visit www.american.edu/soc . Assistant Professorship (Tenure Track) in Entrepreneurship The University of St.Gallen and its School of Management are inviting applications for an Assistant Professorship with Tenure Track in Entrepreneurship, including SME or Family Business. The triple accredited (EQUIS, AACSB, AMBA) university offers a stimulating and well-equipped research environment with a large network ranging from start-ups, small businesses and family firms to large corporations, providing outstanding opportunities for research and collaboration. The new professorship in the School of Management will be invited to become part of the Swiss Research Institute of Small Business and Entrepreneurship (KMU-HSG). Applicants should therefore demonstrate outstanding academic potential and the ability to develop into an internationally recognized scholar. The position involves teaching at Bachelor and Master levels in English. The successful candidate will contribute to the School's teaching portfolio in areas such as Entrepreneurship, Small Business Management, Family Business, and related subjects. We are looking for candidates with excellent teaching skills who are committed to developing innovative teaching formats and inspiring students at all levels. expanding access to high-quality and affordable healthcare, and
fostering authentic community engagement and integration. UTRGV is a distributed campus, one university spanning four

jobs.detailText: Tenure-Track Faculty Position in Management All ranks ( Assistant , Associate , or Full Professor ). Beginning Fall 2027. SKK GSB invites applications for one or more tenure-track faculty position s in Management, at any rank, with the appointment beginning in Fall 2027. SKK GSB is home to a leading global MBA program in Korea , in the heart of Seoul, with an internationally recruited faculty and full-time MBA students from more than 25 countries. All instruction is in English; knowledge of Korean is not required. THE POSITION We welcome applications in all areas of m anagement , micro and macro. Candidates must hold a doctoral degree in management or a related field prior to appointment. We seek colleagues with a strong record of, or clear trajectory toward, publication in the top-tier journals in the field. Research excellence is the primary criterion for this appointment. We also care deeply about teaching, as our MBA programs are at the heart of the school, and we are looking for a colleague who will be an engaging and committed educator in the classroom. Across its programs, SKK GSB is building distinctive strength at the intersection of technology and management, including through its AI MBA program and its developing AI and Business Innovation Lab (AIBIL). WHAT WE OFFER · Supportive research environment: a low teaching load, minimal service and administrative burden for tenure-track faculty, summer research support, and generous funding for research and conference attendance . · Competitive compensation with substantial support for international faculty: housing assistance, preferential expatriate tax treatment, international-school tuition support for children, medical insurance, and relocation coverage. · A genuinely international, English-medium academic community engaged with the frontier of business research . · Seoul: a safe, connected, and culturally rich global city that international faculty and their families find genuinely livable, with the school located in its cultural heart. ABOUT THE SCHOOL SKK GSB was established in 2004 with the support of the Samsung Foundation, with the mission of building a world-class MBA program in Korea. Part of Sungkyunkwan University, one of Asia's oldest institutions with more than 600 years of history, SKK GSB is AACSB-accredited. Our internationally recruited faculty publish in the leading journals in their fields; our full-time MBA students come from across Asia, Europe, Africa, and the Americas. Alongside the flagship full-time MBA, the school offers a professional MBA program, a joint Executive MBA with Indiana University's Kelley School of Business, an MMS program with EDHEC and UC Berkeley, and specialized Business Analytics and AI MBA programs. TO APPLY Please send a cover letter, curriculum vitae, a representative sample of research paper s , and evidence of teaching effectiveness to [email protected] . Reference letters will be requested for short-listed candidates. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. Faculty Search Committee, SKK GSB, Sungkyunkwan University Email: [email protected] Web: gsb.skku.edu Sungkyunkwan University is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.detailText: Founded in 1850, the University of Rochester is one of the nation's leading research institutions and one of the top universities in the world for entrepreneurs. It is a member of the Association of American Universities and ranked 49th by U.S. News & World Report (2027) among national universities and 127th globally by Times of Higher Education . University faculty, scholars, artists, alumni, and students have revolutionized their fields, discovering ways to address the world's biggest challenges, earning notable recognitions including Nobel Prizes, Pulitzer Prizes, Grammy Awards, and Guggenheim and MacArthur Fellowships. The University's diverse community includes more than 3,900 full and part-time faculty members and nearly 12,000 students. Founded in 1958, Simon Business School offers undergraduate, MBA, specialized master’s, executive, online, and doctoral education. Its academic identity is grounded in an economics-based, analytical approach to business and a longstanding commitment to rigorous research. Simon develops analytical and adaptive problem-solvers who lead ideas and industries forward. The School’s top-ranked programs combine quantitative depth with strategic responsiveness, preparing graduates to turn insight into value-driving action. With deep connections across sectors, its global community is transforming the future of business. Simon today offers a broad portfolio of business education spanning the undergraduate through doctoral levels. Its graduate offerings include the Full-Time, Professional, and Executive MBA programs; specialized MS programs in Accountancy, Artificial Intelligence in Business, Business Analytics, Finance, Management, and Marketing Analytics; an MS in Medical Management; online programs; a PhD program and a Doctor of Business Administration. Simon recently forged partnerships with six colleges and universities, enabling students to earn a master’s degree in business in just one year after completing their undergraduate studies through the 4+1 Business Master’s Pathway program. Simon is intentionally small and highly personalized. The Full-Time MBA class entering in fall 2026 numbered 84 students representing 21 countries, with an average of five years of professional experience. The School’s specialized master’s programs add a substantial and globally diverse student population. Simon’s alumni community numbers approximately 19,000 and includes senior leaders in business and industry around the world. The School is entering an important new chapter with undergraduate business education now housed within Simon, thereby creating an opportunity to build a more integrated continuum of undergraduate and graduate business education and to deepen connections across the University of Rochester. Simon is particularly well positioned to leverage the University’s strengths in medicine and health care, engineering, data science and AI, entrepreneurship, the arts, and the growing innovation economy of Rochester and Western New York. Research is deeply embedded in Simon’s history and culture. The School has made important contributions to the fields of finance, accounting, economics, marketing, and organizational decision-making, and its faculty continue to produce influential scholarship across business disciplines. Three leading academic journals — the Journal of Financial Economics , Journal of Accounting & Economics , and Journal of Monetary Economics — were founded at the University of Rochester, reflecting the institution’s longstanding influence on modern economic and financial thought. Simon combines the resources and intellectual ambition of a leading research university with the intimacy of a relatively small business school. Its close-knit community, accessible faculty, highly engaged alumni, and longstanding international orientation have been defining features of the Simon experience. As the School looks to its future, it does so from a position of distinctive academic strength and with an opportunity to reimagine how that heritage can serve the rapidly changing needs of students, employers, and the business sector. Current rankings and outcomes include the following: #26 among U.S. business schools --- Bloomberg Businessweek , 2026 #34 among U.S. business schools — S. News & World Report , 2026 #29 among U.S. business schools — Financial Times , 2026 #2 in the U.S. for salary growth — Financial Times , 2026 #6 for ROI among top-35 U.S. business schools — Bloomberg Businessweek , 2025 #21 among US business schools and #37 globally in Linked In’s 2026 Top MBA Programs URochester is ranked #49 in US News and World Report for 2026 88% of job-seeking Full-Time MBA Class of 2025 graduates accepted employment within three months of graduation $162K average starting compensation for the Full-Time MBA Class of 2025 The Simon Business School Dean reports to the Provost and Chief Academic Officer and is a member of the University Deans’ Council and the President’s University Cabinet. The next Dean will have the opportunity to lead Simon’s next chapter, inheriting a distinguished research legacy, a strong faculty, an engaged alumni community, an expanded undergraduate mandate, and an opportunity to define a differentiated model for business education at a time of profound change in both higher education and the global economy. Academic candidates will be expected to hold credentials for appointment at the level of full professor. Nontraditional candidates should demonstrate a high level of professional success and a deep appreciation of the academic research mission. Nominations, inquiries, and expressions of interest should be sent to: [email protected] . At the University of Rochester, we are committed to fostering, cultivating, and preserving an inclusive and welcoming culture and are united by a strong commitment to be ever better—Meliora. It is an ideal that informs our shared mission to ensure all members of our community feel safe, respected, included, and valued. The base salary range for this position is $700,000 to $950,000 with final determination of compensation made after consideration of qualifications and experience.

jobs.detailText: The Dispute Resolution Research Center at the Kellogg School of Management, Northwestern University, is seeking applicants for our notable postdoctoral fellowship. The primary criterion for acceptance is research excellence relevant to conflict or cooperation, broadly defined. The position is slated to start in September of 2027 and last for approximately three years. Salary is competitive, and the position will have access to research funding, including for independent projects. Applicants must have completed a PhD in a social science discipline (e.g., organizational behavior, sociology, psychology, economics) — or in a related discipline that can inform the social sciences (e.g., a “big data” discipline) — prior to the beginning of the fellowship. The fellow will conduct original research with one or more faculty members at Kellogg. Learn about our current and past postdoctoral fellows here . As the DRRC works closely with faculty in the Management and Organizations (MORS) department, applicants are encouraged to identify one or more MORS faculty members with whom they would be interested in collaborating. The fellow is expected to become actively involved in MORS and DRRC intellectual communities by regularly participating in colloquia, workshops and research seminars. The fellow is also welcome to audit PhD courses. For full consideration, please submit application materials by Sunday, November 15, 2026. You will need to submit: (1) a cover letter identifying at least one faculty member with whom you would be interested in collaborating (2) a current CV (3) a research statement that makes clear how your work is relevant to conflict or cooperation (4) up to two publications or manuscripts (5) the names and contact information for 2–3 people who will submit recommendation letters on your behalf Click here to apply. Northwestern University is an equal opportunity employer. Hiring is contingent upon eligibility to work in the United States.

The search committee will assess candidates’ qualifications and ultimately determine the appropriate appointment type and rank. Northern Illinois University is a comprehensive research university with about 16,000 students. The main campus is located in DeKalb, Illinois, approximately 65 miles west of downtown Chicago. Recognized by Poets and Quants as one of the top 100 undergraduate business schools in the U.S. and No. 2 in Illinois, the NIU College of Business is AACSB accredited in both business and accounting. The college currently serves approximately 2,800 students in our undergraduate and graduate programs. On campus, the Department of Management offers undergraduate degrees in Human Resource Management, Leadership, Entrepreneurship, and Business Administration. In addition, we teach extensively in graduate programs located in DeKalb, Chicago, Schaumburg, Naperville, and a number of international locations. Our eleven tenure-track and three full-time non-tenure-track faculty members include a Presidential Research Professor, two University-level teaching award winners, many College-level teaching award winners, and numerous thought leaders in their fields. We offer a diverse and collegial culture that is deeply committed to rigorous, high-quality education and impactful research. The department is tightly linked to the entrepreneurial ecosystem both within the University and in our surrounding communities, and places great value on collaboration. Position SummaryPrimary teaching responsibilities will be in entrepreneurship (Creativity, Business Model Development, Social Entrepreneurship, etc.) and strategic management at the undergraduate, graduate, and executive levels. In addition to teaching, tenure-track and tenured faculty will be expected to publish high-quality and impactful research, provide service to the Department, College, and University, and engage with the broader business community. The expectations for a non-tenure-track faculty member are similar, without the requirement for research.

The successful candidate will be a collaborative and forward-thinking leader with the leadership, management, fundraising, and scholarly abilities necessary to succeed as the Dean of the School of
jobs.detailText: DEAN, SCHOOL OF BUSINESS The University of Connecticut (UConn), one of the nation’s leading public research universities, seeks a visionary and dynamic leader to serve as Dean of the School of Business . The successful candidate will be a collaborative and forward-thinking leader with the leadership, management, fundraising, and scholarly abilities necessary to succeed as the Dean of the School of Business. Founded in 1881, UConn is a Land Grant and Sea Grant institution and member of the Space Grant Consortium. The University is the state’s flagship institution of higher education and includes seven campuses across the state: Avery Point, Hartford, Stamford, Storrs, and Waterbury, the Law School in Hartford, and UConn Health in Farmington. UConn has approximately 10,000 faculty and staff and 32,000 students, including more than 24,000 undergraduates and nearly 8,000 graduate and professional students. Record numbers of undergraduate applications and support for student success have enabled the University to become extraordinarily selective. The Dean will be the School’s public voice, promoting initiatives within UConn and across the state and articulating the School’s contributions at the local, state, regional, national, and international levels. Working collaboratively with all stakeholders in the university community, the Dean will support excellence and creativity in teaching, research, innovation, entrepreneurship, and service while fostering activities that improve the retention, achievement, entrepreneurship, and timely graduation of students. Additionally, the Dean will work with external sponsors, funding agencies, and industry and community leaders to develop research and educational partnerships that contribute to the economic vitality of the state and nation. The Dean will effectively steward the School’s and University’s resources, overseeing the management of budgets, endowments, space, and personnel. In pursuing these responsibilities, the Dean, who reports to the Provost, will work collaboratively with the University’s senior leadership as well as the School’s faculty and staff. The successful candidate will be a nationally recognized, innovative leader prepared to advance the initiatives and priorities contained in the University’s strategic plan and able to inspire and engage the School of Business community, including faculty, students, staff, alumni, and supporters. The successful candidate will be expected to broaden participation among members of under-represented groups and advance the School’s national and international reputation as demonstrated through improved rankings, successful fundraising, community engagement, and faculty and student achievement. In addition, the ideal candidate will be dedicated to collaborative governance, will possess a leadership style that values excellence and differences in opinions and experiences, will be a skilled administrator capable of building strong working relationships, and will be able to imagine new possibilities for the School. Minimum Qualifications Credentials that merit appointment for a tenure-track academic appointment at the rank of Professor or a current appointment at UConn at the rank of Professor in one of UConn’s schools and colleges, including a doctoral degree or other terminal degree in a field relevant to leadership in academic affairs and the school. Equivalent foreign degrees are acceptable. Demonstrated visionary leadership with a proven track record of successful administrative leadership. Progressively responsible leadership experience at a higher education institution, demonstrating knowledge of core management functions, experience with managing strategic priorities, and understanding and embracing University policies, guidance, best practices, and procedures. Success in building and executing a strategic and fiscally sound academic budget. Solid track record in meeting a university mission with respect to enrollment, graduation, research, innovation, and fundraising. Preferred Qualifications Background and experience pertinent to the unique programs and setting of the School, including a clear understanding of the academic vision of the university, the land-grant mission of the University, and the School’s goals and opportunities to deliver quality undergraduate and graduate education. Professional experience in or with business or industry outside higher education, including: demonstrated responsibility for organizational growth, innovation, financial performance, or the development of new markets, products, or revenue streams; or significant partnerships resulting in increased student engagement and placement, new research, or adoption of technology. Proven business and political acumen commensurate with the leadership needs of the School of Business, including the ability to navigate the organizational, political, and fiscal realities unique to a major public research university; demonstrable experience applying sound judgment; and an ability to manage change, resolve conflict, and build consensus. Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to develop, engage, and maintain constructive and professional relationships with senior administrators, faculty, staff, students, and other individuals and organizations. A collaborative and collegial approach toward fostering partnerships within the School of Business and academic units across the University. Demonstrated commitment to increasing a sense of belonging for all members of the school, including assessing needs, developing initiatives, and applying best practices. Demonstrated understanding of the Dean’s role as chief fundraiser for the School of Business and the skillsets needed to form and maintain partnerships with donors and alumni. Varied and extensive success in securing extramural funding from state and federal agencies or foundations. Demonstrated record of academic leadership that advances excellence across the School’s core missions of research, teaching, student success, external engagement, and societal impact, including the ability to recruit, develop, and retain outstanding faculty and staff. Knowledge of AACSB accreditation standards and experience with accreditation, continuous improvement, assurance of learning, faculty sufficiency and qualifications, and strategic planning within an AACSB-accredited business school. The Department offers bachelor's degrees in Cinema Studies (with tracks in Production and Critical Studies) and Communication (with tracks in Corporate Communication, Design and Digital Media, Journalism, and Media Studies). The Department has a strong commitment to interdisciplinary inquiry and welcomes candidates whose work crosses traditional boundaries. We seek a candidate with the range to teach across both production and critical studies, grounded in a strong command of film and media history and theory. Given the rapidly evolving digital media landscape, the ideal candidate engages with diverse modes of production and brings a deep understanding of the craft alongside its social, cultural, political, and aesthetic dimensions. Candidates whose scholarship focuses on national, global, diasporic, African American, or LGBTQ+ cinemas are also welcome to apply. QUALIFICATIONS Candidates must hold an MFA or PhD. ABD candidates are eligible provided the degree is conferred prior to appointment. Preferred qualifications include: The successful candidate will have a demonstrated commitment to excellence in undergraduate teaching as well as an active and developing research and creative practice. Candidates must demonstrate the ability to teach and mentor students in narrative, documentary, and experimental film and video production. The successful candidate will be expected to teach across these areas, advise senior production projects, and contribute actively to curriculum development and program review. We also provide mentoring and support for research, scholarship, and publication as part of our commitment to ongoing faculty professional development. Send job Job Details Assistant Professor in Media Studies The Department of Communication Studies in the College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB) invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor in Media Studies to begin August 2027. We seek applications from candidates with a strong background in critical media studies and the ability to teach multimedia production (preferred areas include broadcasting, digital media, film, or multimedia journalism). The teaching load will be four courses per year over two semesters (2/2). Areas of specialization may include Digital Media, Advertising, Visual Storytelling, Interactive Digital Narrative, and related emerging media fields. Versatility in teaching media courses is desirable, as the successful candidate will support multiple concentrations within the media curriculum. Instruction may include both in-person and online delivery formats. A terminal degree (PhD or MFA) by August 15, 2027, is required. Ideal qualifications include a degree in Media, Communication Studies, or a closely related field; a record of publications or the potential for conducting research; a record of effective instruction or the potential to effectively teach. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to our department by teaching a variety of courses in our undergraduate and graduate degree programs and developing classes in their own areas of expertise. The College of Arts and Sciences (CAS) is home to 19 academic departments and six Centers and Institutes. Our 19 departments — home to over 300 full-time faculty and more than 58 baccalaureate, master’s, and doctoral degrees — make us the largest academic entity in the UAB academic enterprise. We are home to research centers, community outreach programs, and interdisciplinary cooperation. The University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB) is a research university and academic health center that discovers, teaches, and applies knowledge for the intellectual, cultural, social, and economic benefit of Birmingham, the state, and beyond. UAB is internationally renowned for its intensely collaborative culture that has — for more than five decades — produced breakthroughs in education, health care, research, and service. UAB was ranked #1 in the United States for 2018 and 2019 in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings, Young University Rankings. In 2021, Forbes named UAB as America’s No. 1 Best Large Employer, topping a list of more than 500 public and private corporations, hospitals, universities, Fortune 500 companies and more, across dozens of industries. Most recently, UAB earned the distinction of being named to the 2025 Great Colleges to Work For Honor Roll. Review of applications will begin immediately, and all applications submitted by October 26, 2026, will receive full consideration. Campus interviews are anticipated to be scheduled in early December. All applications should be submitted online and include the following documents: A two-to-three-page cover letter that specifically addresses your qualifications, research, and teaching experience Curriculum Vitae Teaching portfolio that includes your teaching philosophy, syllabi of courses taught, summaries of course evaluations, and other evidence of effective instruction Additional materials that demonstrate your experience in media, such as creative portfolios, recently completed media projects, and representative media publications The names and email addresses for three professional references Interested applicants please follow this link to apply: https://uab.peopleadmin.com/postings/28462 Please address your cover letter to Alan Franks and contact him at alfranks@uab.edu if you have any questions about the position. UAB is an Equal Employment/Equal Educational Opportunity Institution dedicated to providing equal opportunities and equal access to all individuals regardless of race, color, religion, ethnic or national origin, sex (including pregnancy), genetic information, age, disability, religion, and veteran’s status. As required by Title IX, UAB prohibits sex discrimination in any education program or activity that it operates. Individuals may report concerns or questions to UAB’s Assistant Vice President and Senior Title IX Coordinator. The Title IX notice of nondiscrimination is located at uab.edu/titleix . A pre-employment background check investigation is performed on candidates selected for employment. jobs.title: Tenure-Track/Tenured (Open Rank) Faculty Position in Interpersonal Communication (INTERVIEW APPLICATIONS SENT)
statuses: Job Description: The Department of Communication at Rutgers University's School of Communication and Information seeks a full-time faculty member in interpersonal communication. The search is open rank but prioritizes early career scholars. The appointment will begin Fall 2027. We are looking for a scholar of interpersonal communication who conducts applied empirical research in complex social and relational contexts. We welcome applicants who approach their scholarship from a diverse range of empirical perspectives (e.g., quantitative analysis, qualitative analysis, conversation analysis). Research and teaching interests should address contemporary communication problems such as facilitating difficult or high-stakes conversations in personal, family, professional, or community contexts. This might include such topics as discussing social problems and differences, engaging in interpersonal influence, managing conflict, communicating support or advice, or negotiating human relationships in personal or professional contexts, in face-to-face or technologically mediated channels. The candidate should have a research program that is theory-driven, data-informed, and communication-centered. We prioritize applicants who are active in the communication discipline.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Media Psychology (Review Begins: 9/11/2026, INTERVIEWS SCHEDULED)
statuses: Job Description: The Department of Communication and Media at the University of Michigan (Ann Arbor) seeks to hire a full-time, tenure-track assistant professor to teach and conduct research in media psychology, to begin August 25, 2027. The preferred candidate will demonstrate an innovative research agenda that advances the understanding of media psychology (i.e., uses, processes and effects) at the individual, community, and/or societal level. We are particularly interested in applicants who use innovative methods and approaches in their research and teaching, including experiments, surveys, content analysis, meta-analysis, computational methods, psychophysiological methods, neuroimaging or other social scientific techniques. Scholars utilizing a range of methods, and/or who supplement quantitative methods with qualitative approaches, are welcome. The ideal candidate will provide graduate and undergraduate students with the theoretical and methodological foundations to explore how individuals and groups of people interact with, and are affected by, mediated communication. This may include the processes and effects of media use in relation to a person’s identity, attention, stage of development, or other contextual factors; choices for exposure; and how people’s emotions, cognition and perceptions interact with media—both as recipients and as active users. All areas of media psychology will be considered. This could include scholarship on media choice; psychological antecedents and consequences of media use; representations of gender and/or sexuality and their consequences; representations of race and ethnicity and their consequences; media uses and effects among members of understudied and/or marginalized groups; media uses and effects through the life course; media effects on health, risk, and environmental behavior; media effects on cognitive processing and learning; media and children; media and well-being; new and emerging media (e.g., social media, virtual reality, AI, etc.).

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Strategic Communication (Deadline: 10/21/2026)
statuses: Job Description: The Hubbard School of Journalism and Mass Communication in the College of Liberal Arts invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track faculty position to begin fall semester 2027 (08/30/2027). We are seeking an outstanding scholar with research and teaching experience that address contemporary issues in public relations and the strategic communication professions. An ideal candidate should have a research agenda that centers issues of public relations in the context of artificial intelligence and/or social media. This agenda may relate to areas such as (but not limited to) corporate social responsibility, public relations management, activist public relations, and crisis and risk communication. A preference will be given to individuals with professional experience in public relations/communications. The successful candidates for this position will show outstanding promise and/or evidence of sustaining a vigorous program of original research and publication with potential for external funding; show promise and/or evidence of excellence in undergraduate and graduate teaching and advising (both M.A. and Ph. D.); and demonstrate the capacity and commitment to teach undergraduate courses in the areas of strategic communication case analysis, strategic communication campaigns, management for strategic communication, digital strategy for strategic communication, professional writing for strategic communication, and other strategic communication skills courses. The ability to contribute to the graduate curriculum in areas related to theory and research in public relations and advanced methods is preferred. Professional experience and the capacity to contribute to the ongoing development and delivery of a rapidly evolving AI and emerging-media focused professional curriculum is also preferred.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Strategic Communication (Review begins: 10/15/2026)
statuses: Job Description: Northwestern College seeks applicants for a full-time, tenure-track position at the rank of assistant professor in our English and communications department to begin August 2027. Interested candidates who have already attained higher rank may also inquire. The successful candidate can expect to teach courses in communications with specific emphases in strategic communication and public relations. The teaching load for this position is 24 credit-hours per academic year, normally three to four courses per semester. Responsibilities include teaching introductory and intermediate courses in communication, along with advanced courses in public relations. While the primary focus of this position is strategic communication, strongest consideration will be given to those who also have additional experience in public relations. In your letter, (1) summarize your teaching experience; (2) describe your scholarly trajectory; and (3) discuss how our Christian Identity Statement would inform and shape your teaching and scholarship.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Social and Digital Media in Journalism (Deadline: 10/15/2026)
statuses: Job Description: The School of Journalism and Strategic Media (SJSM) in the Fulbright College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Arkansas invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Social and Digital Media in Journalism to start in August 2027. This is a standard nine-month faculty appointment. SJSM seeks a scholar of Social and Digital Media with familiarity of the professional practice of social and digital media in journalism. SJSM is particularly interested in candidates whose areas of focus expand into any of the following: strategic communication, digital and platform cultures, media audiences and engagement, online communities, influencers and creators, digital advertising and public relations, algorithms and platforms, artificial intelligence and media, misinformation, or the social and cultural implications of digital media. The successful candidate will maintain an active program of research and/or scholarly/creative activity and contribute to the School's undergraduate and graduate curricula. Teaching responsibilities may include existing courses in social and digital media as well as courses in the candidate's areas of expertise across the School's journalism, multimedia, and advertising/public relations programs. The successful candidate will have opportunities to develop new courses that complement and expand the School's curriculum in social and digital media. The position carries a 2-2 teaching load and includes requirements for research and service. Faculty hired in this position will have an opportunity to be a part of Fulbright College’s multidisciplinary Democracy as a Public Good cluster hire at the University of Arkansas.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Communication (Deadline: 10/10/2026)
statuses: Job Description: The Department of Communication in the Fulbright College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Arkansas invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in the area of Communication and Democracy to start in August 2027. In addition to having a research and teaching focus in areas pertaining to Communication and Democracy, applicants should have a focus in rhetoric, dialogue, and deliberation. Faculty hired in this position will have an opportunity to be a part of Fulbright College’s multidisciplinary Democracy as a Public Good cluster hire at the University of Arkansas. Building on existing campus expertise in issues ranging from norms of democratic communication, free speech, media ethics and literacy, humanitarian governance and civil society, risks that AI poses to democratic governance, immigration, and public law, new faculty members participating in the cluster will advance their research agendas through mentoring and opportunities for collaboration—both with other scholars and with communities in the state—that may result in peer-reviewed publications, external funding, and new approaches to the pressing challenges that democracy faces. Competitive applicants will also demonstrate an ability to provide strategic direction and collaboration with our Center for Communication Research, as well as success in working with interdisciplinary research teams, mentoring undergraduate and graduate students, and engaging regional, state, and national funding agencies.

statuses: Job Description: The Department of Communication and Journalism in the College of Arts & Sciences at Texas A&M University invites applications for a tenured Associate Professor in the Communication & Media Science Division. This position is part of a strategic faculty cluster examining the communicative foundations of democratic society. Through coordinated hiring across the department's three academic three academic divisions—Humanities & Critical/Cultural Studies, Communication & Media Science, and Journalism & Media Practices. We seek a scholar whose research advances communication science through rigorous empirical investigations of communication processes in democratic society. Competitive candidates will maintain an established and impactful program of research examining how contemporary media and communication environments shape the production and circulation of public information, as well as the ways individuals and communities evaluate competing public claims, form political and civic judgments, build trust, negotiate disagreement, and participate in public life. Areas of scholarly interest include, but are not limited to, political communication, public opinion, media effects, civic engagement, misinformation, communication and public knowledge, democratic deliberation, and related areas that deepen understanding of communication's role in democratic culture and institutions. We welcome scholars employing diverse empirical approaches whose work is united by a strong theoretical commitment to explaining communication processes.

Applicants should demonstrate strong qualitative and/or quantitative methodological expertise and possess a clearly defined, active research trajectory that reflects a consistent, empirical approach to studying communication in areas relevant to advertising. Applicants should also display evidence of or potential for external funding; the ability to teach core and elective existing courses in our advertising majors; and a commitment to mentoring undergraduate and graduate students. We seek candidates whose research focus complements and/or strengthens the department’s existing expertise. We also welcome applicants whose innovative research expands the department’s scholarly reach and opens new avenues for inquiry in advertising and related fields. In particular, we encourage applications from scholars whose work explores the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI) and advertising, including its implications for communication strategies, consumer outcomes, society, and media effects.

(4) A record of successful teaching as the instructor of record for university-level courses in public relations or courses in a closely related field in strategic communication.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor - Humanities & Critical/Cultural Studies Division (Review Begins: 10/05/2026)
statuses: Job Description: The Department of Communication and Journalism in the College of Arts & Sciences at Texas A&M University invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in the Humanities & Critical/Cultural Studies Division. This position is part of a strategic faculty cluster examining the communicative foundations of democratic society. Through coordinated hiring across the department's three academic three academic divisions—Humanities & Critical/Cultural Studies, Communication & Media Science, and Journalism & Media Practices. We seek a scholar whose research advances humanistic and critical scholarship in communication through the study of communication, rhetoric, and/or media as constitutive of democratic public life. Competitive candidates will demonstrate a promising and sophisticated program of scholarship examining how communicative practices shape public narratives, civic identity, democratic culture, collective memory, public argument, or participation in civic life. Areas of scholarly interest include, but are not limited to, rhetoric, political discourse, democratic culture, media and public culture, citizenship, civic identity, public memory, publics and counter-publics, social movements, and related areas that deepen understanding of communication's role in democratic culture. We welcome scholars employing diverse humanistic, interpretive, historical, qualitative, critical, rhetorical, textual, ethnographic, and related approaches whose work is united by a strong theoretical commitment to understanding communication and democratic practices.
